links.reason: The two decade poems share the frame (அம்ம வாழி தோழி ... என்னாதவ்வே) and differ exactly as the note says: the beasts in 332 should have stated a rule (கொடிதே காதலிப் பிரிதல்), the birds in 333 should have offered their own case (யாஅம் துணைபுணர்ந்து உறைதும் யாங்குப் பிரிந்து உறைதி). Precept against example is a real, specific progression the pair shows.

The verbal echo is real: Kali 61.11-12 (ஈதல் இரந்தார்க்கு ஒன்று ஆற்றாது வாழ்தலின் சாதலும் கூடுமாம்) restates Kural 230 (சாதலின் இன்னாதது இல்லை ... ஈதல் இயையாக் கடை). But teaches claims the ethic 'obliges the girl to yield'; the poem does not say so: the friend laughs at him as shameless (நாண் இலன் மன்ற இவன்) and the close turns on the father's heart, so the 'trap' is the proposer's construction.

Same poet and same patron's death: Patitruppattu 61 names Pari gone to the land of no return (வாராச் சேண்புலம் படர்ந்தோன்) and Kapilar's arrival at the Chera camp for a fame of giving without regret (ஈத்தது இரங்கான்), while Puram 236 asks fate to let him live with Pari in the next birth (உம்மை ... உடன்உறைவு ஆக்குக). The two responses to one loss are specific and the note is accurate.

The shared sign (வளை ஞெகிழ, சாஅய் ... தோள; பைந்தொடி சோரும் ... தோள்) is the stock symptom of separation in akam, so the pairing as such is a shared topic. What teaches adds, the reproach carried by the repeated அணிந்தன்று (ford adorned with flowers, shoulders adorned with loneliness), is all in Kuruntokai 50 and owes nothing to the couplet.

Both have the heart go after the departed man (இறந்தோர் தேஎத்துச் சென்ற நெஞ்சம்; பிரிந்தவர் பின்செல்வாய்), and the contrast of calling it a fool versus asking why it lingers is real. But it rests on reading நீடிய பொருளே as the heart's delay, and the Sangam poem does not limit the Kural's judgment so much as take the heart's flight further; qualifies overstates the relation.

The heart's argument in Kuruntokai 63 (ஈதலும் துய்த்தலும் இல்லோர்க்கு இல்) is the puram maxim of 189 (செல்வத்துப் பயனே ஈதல்; துய்ப்பேம் எனினே), and the man answers it with the one cost it ignores (அம்மா அரிவையும் வருமோ). The pair shows the giving ethic as the cause of separation, which neither verse says alone.

The image is the same act in near-identical words: துன்னற் சிதாஅர் நீக்கித் ... பட்டுடை நல்கி against சிதைந்த சிதாஅர் களைந்து வெளியது உடீஇ. The guide's forecast before the bard asks (கையது கேளா அளவை) set beside Aruvanthai's unasked gift supports the inference that re-dressing the bard was a set first act of reception.

Both turn on a flowering that comes before the promised rains (பருவம் வாரா அளவை ... வம்ப மாரியைக் காரென மதித்தே; கனைதுளி சிந்தாமைப் பூத்து), and the friend's denial of the sign against the heroine's reading of it as a decree (வருந்தே என்றாய் நீ வரைந்து) is a real difference. But 114's first line (பாத்து ... காத்து) is unclear and வருந்தே can be read as a prohibition, so the contrast depends on one reading.

links.reason: The two venbas share an opening line (பொய்கைநல் லூரன் திறன்கிளப்ப / திறங்கிளத்தல் என்னுடைய) and end on the little son as hers (எனக்குடைமை; சிறுவன் உடையேன் துணை). The idyll itself names the deceit and the draining (மாயப் பொய்பல கூட்டிக் கவவுக்கரந்து, வளந்தப வாங்கி) inside its picture of the night city, and Kural 913 condemns the same false embrace (பொய்ம்மை முயக்கம்) as clasping a stranger's corpse. The pair shows one practice admitted in praise and condemned in ethics, which is specific.

Both are the man speaking to his heart about wealth and love (வாரேன் வாழிய நெஞ்சே; அழிதகவு உடைமதி வாழிய நெஞ்சே), a real connection. But Akananuru 123 does not treat staying as cowardice: it rebukes the heart for swinging between going and staying like the tide (ஒன்றிற் கொள்ளாய்), and its man is already on the road (இடைச்சுரத்து), so there is no incompatible claim, and the Pattinappalai's refusal does not answer that reproach.

The wife's justification (பிறர்க்கு என முயலும் பேர் அருள் நெஞ்சமொடு ... பொருட் பிணி போகிய) is the Kural's rule that wealth won by effort is for giving (தாளாற்றித் தந்த பொருளெல்லாம் ... வேளாண்மை செய்தற் பொருட்டு). Seeing the didactic rule used by the wife to make the paalai journey honourable is specific to this pair.

The son's prattle as relief is in both (மழலைவாய் கட்டுரையால்; மருந்து ஓவா நெஞ்சிற்கு அமிழ்தம் அயின்றற்றா), so the link is real. But the quoted 'நோய் நாம் தணிக்கும் மருந்து' is the bard's praise in Kali 81.18, and in Kali 81 the words the street women taught the boy (ஞாயர் பயிற்ற) bring the other houses into hers; nothing shows the chatter carrying the father home, and the venba says nothing of street words.
links.text_issue: Both verses flagged uncertain; Kali 81 speaker division and ஏனாதிப்பாடியம் are obscure.

links.reason: Both mark the end of shared bathing (அருவி நம்மோடு ஆடல் ... அரிய ஆகுதல்; பாய்புஉடன் ஆடாமையின் கலுழ்புஇல தேறி), a real link. But 224 does not say the change is his neglect: அவர்க்கு இனி அரிய can as well follow from her being kept at home, which is Akananuru 38's situation, so the contrast teaches builds between neglect and confinement depends on one reading.

Both are the friend's disclosure to the mother (இவட்கு அமைந்தனன் ... in 103; உரைத்தனென் அல்லனோ அஃதென் யாய்க்கே in 280), a set situation shared by two decades. 280's reproach that she spoke on the strength of his word (வரைந்தனை நீ எனக் கேட்டு) is real, but the pair adds little beyond the shared situation; the 'price' comes from 280 alone.

Kural 1081 asks what she is (அணங்குகொல் ஆய்மயில் கொல்லோ ... மாதர்கொல்), Natrinai 8 whose she is (யார் மகள்கொல் இவள் தந்தை வாழியர்) and blesses her mother, so the pairing shows wonder turning to kin, a specific point. The note's 'first sight' is loose: the colophon places Natrinai 8 at the end of the first union, seeing her again among companions, though the contrast still stands.

The shared formula is exact (செவ் வேர்ப் பலவின் பயம் கெழு கொல்லி) with the god-made Kolli figure (மாயா இயற்கைப் பாவை; நிலைபெறு கடவுள் ஆக்கிய பலர்புகழ் பாவை), and both answer a doubter. But only 201 uses the figure's permanence (unmoved by wind, rain, thunder, quake); 209 compares her beauty to a famed figure, so 'lends its one property, that it does not perish' to both is generous.

Both feel the storm as aimed at one woman (இன்னுயிர் குறித்தே; ஒருத்தி திறத்து), a specific shared turn. That the venba moves it into the friend's mouth rests on its colophon thurai (தோழி தனது ஆற்றாமை தோன்ற உரைத்தது), not on the verse, which could be the heroine speaking of herself as 'one woman'; and two instances do not make a 'formula'.
links.text_issue: Kar Narpathu 3 line 3 has printed variants (@ இழித்தெழுங் தோங்கும்).

links.reason: The simile is the same (பொருள் இல்லான் இளமை போல் புல்லென்றாள், 38.15; வறியவன் இளமை போல் வாடிய சினைய, 10.1), and 38 does move it from the parched land to the girl, pairing it with its opposite (அருள் வல்லான் ஆக்கம் போல் அணிபெறும்) and a field after rain. The closing gloss about the kali form is grand, but the core observation is accurate and specific.

Kali 143.52-55 (தன் உயிர் போலத் தழீஇ உலகத்து மன் உயிர் காக்கும் இம் மன்னனும் என் கொலோ ... என் உயிர் காவாதது) invokes the puram doctrine of Puram 186 (மன்னன் உயிர்த்தே மலர்தலை உலகம்) and finds the one life the king cannot guard. That limit is a real qualification the pair shows.

The whole contrast rests on one reading of line 4 (காலை யன்ன காலைமுந் துறுத்தே), which the marker flagged and which the Tamil does not fix; on another reading there is no 'evening swallowing morning' at all. The claim that the couplet is 'a later tidying' is a historical story neither verse supports.

The tribute formula is the same in both (யானையொடு அரும்கலம் துறுத்துப் பணிந்துவழி மொழிதல்; நன்கலம் களிற்றொடு ... வணங்கினர் வழிமொழிந்து), and in Akananuru 124 the enemy's submission is the condition of the soldier's homecoming (இன்றே புகுதல் வாய்வது). The pair shows one puram event read from the akam side, which is specific.

The emblems match: conch-white body and plough (மை இல் வால் வளை மேனி ... வளை நாஞ்சில்; கடல் வளர் புரிவளை புரையும் மேனி அடல் வெந் நாஞ்சில்) and the bird banner (சேவல் அம் கொடியோய்; புள்கொடி). Puram 56 counts them among four gods, while the Paripadal addresses them in the singular (ஒருவனை ... கண்ணை ... மேனியை), so the pair shows shared iconography put to different theology.

links.reason: Both open யாயாகியளே and both have the friend tell how the wife hides the man's கொடுமை (நம்மு னாணிக் கரப்பாடும்மே; கரந்தனள் ஆகலின் நாணிய வருமே). The two costs, the wasted body of the unworn flower (பெய்யாப் பூவின் மெய்சாயினளே) and shame at the festival she leads (விழவுமுதலாட்டி), are in the Tamil and specific to the pair.

Near-identical signs (அவல்தொறும் தேரை / அவல்தோறு ... வரிநுணல் கறங்க; கார்தொடங் கின்றால் காலை / கார்தொடங் கின்றே காலை) lead in one to the chariot setting out (தேர்தொடங் கின்றால் நம்வயினானே) and in the other to his not thinking of them (நம்மும் உள்ளார்). That the season does not fix its meaning is a real lesson of the pair.

Kural 1150 welcomes the gossip (யாம்வேண்டும் கெளவை எடுக்கும்இவ் வூர்), while Kuruntokai 302 fears the gossip that they are inseparable has kept him away (பிரியா நண்பினர் இருவரும் என்னும் அலரதற்கு அஞ்சினன் கொல்லோ). On that reading the two make opposite claims about the effect of alar, and the note states the reading.

Both make theology from letters, but by different devices: Kural 1 uses அகரம் as first of the letters (அகர முதல எழுத்தெல்லாம்), Paripadal 2.58-59 the demonstratives அவ்வும் ... உவ்வும் எவ் வயினோயும் as pointing words. Neither extends the other, so develops misfits; the origin-versus-pervasion contrast in teaches is fair.

Both restrain the departing man (அணங்குவளர்த்து அகறல் வல்லாதீமோ; வல்வரவு வாழ்வார்க்குரை), a shared situation. The contrast in teaches is overstated: the couplet has not 'given up persuasion', its threat of death is itself the persuasion, and its speaker is contested, so the pairing yields little beyond the shared situation.

Both concern the velan rite and the true cause of the girl's sickness (முதுவாய் வேலன் 'எம்மிறை அணங்கலின் வந்தன்று இந்நோய்'; வேலனார் போக மறிவிடுக்க). The sequence from private mockery to the friend's disclosure is a stock order of the convention assembled from two unrelated poems, not something either poem points to.

Both use the fear that her waist will snap (செல்வாள் இறும் என்று அஞ்சி; நுகப்பிற்கு நல்ல படாஅ பறை), a stock conceit. Thinaimalai 17's own turn, his heart swaying with her (என்நெஞ்சம் ஒல்கும்வாய் ஒல்கல் உறும்), is real, but line 1 is garbled and the contrast teaches draws comes mostly from the Thinaimalai verse.

links.reason: Both turn on the town's கௌவை (கௌவை ஆகின்றது ஐய நின் நட்பே; யாம்வேண்டும் கெளவை), so the word link is exact, and the colophon of 354 (வரைவு கடாயது) supports the use toward marriage. But the Kural's speaker and addressee come from Parimelazhagar, and the pairing beyond that is the shared topic of alar.

The shared phrase is real: the land's loneliness ends (புலம்பு தீர்ந்து இனிய ஆயின புறவே; மலர்ந்த ஞாலம் புலம்புபுறக் கொடுப்ப). But in Akananuru 4 it is the rain that does this (கார்செய்தன்றே), before the chariot is pointed out, not 'as his chariot comes into view'; the reading of the land's loneliness as hers is generous.

Paripadal 5 refuses wealth and pleasure (பொருளும் பொன்னும் போகமும் அல்ல) and asks grace, love and aram. Paripadal 21's prayer asks that dwelling at the god's feet be granted as today (நின் அடி உறை இன்று போல் இயைக), not that liquor and dancing recur; teaches overreads இன்று போல் to manufacture the opposition.

Both are the friend refusing the night visit and offering the day (இரவின் வாரல் ... பகலும் பெறுவை; இரவின் வருதல் எவனோ பகல்வரின்), and both open on a tusker after a tiger fight (கொடுவரி தாக்கி வென்ற வருத்தமொடு; உழுவையொடு உழந்த ... விழுப்புண்). The different handling, a full day plan in 308 and the sweet-love/bitter-coming refrain in 49 (இனிது - மற்று இன்னாதே), is accurately described.

The shared phrase is real (விருந்து அயர் விருப்பினள்; மாலை அயர்கம் விருந்து). But teaches says each partner ascribed the feast to the other, and in the Kural the man (on Parimelazhagar's reading) wants it for himself, not for her; in Natrinai 374 the guest-feast is the wife's household duty she longs to keep, not a picture of reunion.
links.text_issue: Natrinai 374 line 5 (முற்றையும் உடையமோ) is compressed; marker flagged the sense.

links.reason: The puram name is a real connection: Akananuru 78 recalls Pari with Kapilar beside him driving off the kings (வாய்மொழிக் கபிலன் சூழ ... ஏந்துகோட்டு யானை வேந்தர் ஓட்டிய), the siege of Puram 110 (பறம்பு கொள்ற்கு அரிதே). But the note does not say what the akam poet does with it, which is to make the girl's brow smell of Pari's pool, and it is a shared history rather than a shared image.

The tension needs சிறுமை in 431 to mean desire, which is a commentator's sense; the marked reading has smallness, and 440 speaks of hiding one's loves from enemies (காதல காதல் அறியாமை உய்க்கிற்பின்), a matter of security. 'Removing and hiding are different programmes' only restates the claim.

The key word is shared: Natrinai 23 ends கண்ணே காமம் கரப்பு அரியவ்வே, Kural 1271 opens கரப்பினுங் கையிகந் தொல்லாநின் உண்கண். Natrinai 23 sorts the signs into those an excuse covers (தொடி பழி மறைத்தலின் தோள் உய்ந்தனவே) and the eyes, which do not, so it does supply the ground of the couplet's claim.
links.text_issue: Natrinai 23 line 3 (இடிப்பு மெய்யது ஒன்று உடைத்தே) is hard.

links.reason: Both have the herdsmen's flutes in the rainy evening (குழல் தொடங்கினரே கோவலர்; கல்லாக் கோவலர் கொன்றைஅம் தீம் குழல்), a stock mullai sign. The match is not 'sound for sound' (364 has bells, the north wind, the midnight sky; 371 lightning and her bangles), and nothing in two poems by different poets shows a shared code by which partners knew each other's hour.

Both say speech before unfit hearers is waste (பொருளணர்வா ரில்வழிப் பாட்டுரைத்த லின்னா; தங்கணத்தார் அல்லார்முன் கோட்டி கொளல்), which is agreement, not development. The Innaa verse lists four separate painful things; setting the first beside the fourth as one 'gift wasted on both sides' is read into the list from the repeated பொருள்.

Both pair her loyalty with her loss of colour (உள்ளுவன் ... உரைப்பது அவர்திறம் ... பசப்பு; புகரின்று நயந்தனன் போலும் கவரும் ... மாமைக் கவினே). But in 286 the man is the one who carries off her glow (நாடன் ... கவரும்), with போலும் holding the praise at a distance, so 'never his fault in her own mouth' does not hold, and two verses do not make a fixed rule.

Both tie the drinking order to the front line: in 292 the warrior who would not wait for the toddy (என்முறை வருக என்னான்) will stop the army, in 298 the warrior given the dregs (கலங்கல் தருமே) complains that the king does not say நீ முந்து. The pair shows feast and battle order read together, which is specific.
links.text_issue: Both verses flagged uncertain; 298's poet varies (ஆவியார் / ஆலியார).

poems.note: Bees humming at the kaanthal give one match (union) at most, and humming is sound, not an act.
The bull tossing the herdsman's garland into her hair is the narrated event, not a side image.
Lines 1, 2 and 4 are lost; nothing can be tagged.

iraicchi.act: the doe frolics with its mate in the first rains
iraicchi.sense: as the deer pair rejoice together with the rain, the lovers will be joined now, comforting the heroine that he will come (வருவர் இன்னே).

poems.note: The forest as a stage with kodal hands, bee lute and dancing peacock is an open festive metaphor of the season, not mapped part by part to the lovers.
பாசம்பட்டு ஓடும் may be 'snared' or 'slipping on moss' (cf. பாசிப் பசுஞ்சுனை), so what the monkey's act implies cannot be fixed.
The bees' song is mood; the lines are hard to construe.
The gathering clouds are the season's sign, and her eyes are compared openly to rain.

iraicchi.act: having fed on white paddy, the elephant sleeps on the cool slope instead of roaming
iraicchi.sense: with the rains upon them even the elephant rests at home, so the man too will stay rather than set out.

poems.note: The parrot is the addressee and messenger; striking it removes the poem.
The peacock dances 'like you' (நின்னே போல): an open likeness of look, not an act.

iraicchi.act: the striped bees, having joined and sported in the opened flowers, keep circling their mouths
iraicchi.sense: the bees roving among many blossoms point to the man's roving among the courtesans the poem goes on to name.

poems.note: The lotus opening in dew is tied to a smiling woman by போல, so it is an open comparison.
The herons are compared openly to a king's army (அரைசர் ஒண் படைத் தொகுதியின்); no second correspondence to the lovers can be named.
The shark that tore the net is the stated reason the kin are away, part of the poem's sense.
The trampled neythal is joined to her by போல: an open comparison.
The monkey leaping on the mango for the jackfruit's sweetness has no clear implication for the lovers.
The otter's dawn sleep among flashing vaalai could hint at the sated man, but the poem gives nothing to fix it.
The cock-fight is joined to her pain by போல.
Lines 1 and 2 are mostly lost.
The anril on the palmyra marks the location of her yard, which is the poem's sense.
The monkey drawing milk from the wild cow might map caress and yielding, but neither correspondence is fixed by the Tamil and line 2 is uncertain.

iraicchi.act: the peacock raids the millet the hill girl guards
iraicchi.sense: the guarded field is entered by day, so he need not come at midnight through the beasts; he can come as the peacock does.

poems.note: All the images are joined by போல.

iraicchi.act: the milch cow goes to its calf at evening
iraicchi.sense: everything returns to its own at dusk except him, which is why she says she will not survive.

poems.note: Lines 1 to 3 are hard to construe; no creature acts toward the lovers.
The calling peacocks are what she addresses as fools; they are the poem's subject.
The tiger that missed the elephant pictures the road's danger, not an act of a lover.
The tethered elephant is the vehicle of an open simile (அன்ன) for the bamboo's sound.

iraicchi.act: the birds snatch the fish she was set to guard
iraicchi.sense: while she chased birds from the catch, he snatched her beauty (நுகர்வனன் உண்டான் நலம்).

poems.note: Several creatures going home make a whole scene; the end of the poem is lost.
The plantain bud is given open similes (கடுப்ப, அன்ன).
Children warming hands at gems taken for embers is a look, not a lover's act.
